children: Thailand's monetary policy is fully accommodative and it is not appropriate to reduce interest rates now, though there is still room for further cuts, the central bank said on Thursday.
The current policy interest rate (THCBIR=ECI), at 1.00%, is appropriate for the present situation and for supporting the economy, Bank of Thailand Governor Vitai Ratanakorn told a business forum.
There is still room for a further 0.5 percentage point reduction, but keeping interest rates low for too long could hurt savers, he said.
There are other policy tools available if additional support for the economy is needed, Vitai said, adding that the economy faced structural problems that could not be resolved by any single measure.
Thailand's high household debt means that monetary policy cannot provide much economic stimulus because it cannot generate demand, Vitai said.
The current weakness of the economy is the result of scars from past shocks, which have become more frequent, he said.
The country's potential growth rate stands at 2.7%, and efforts should focus on lifting actual growth closer to that potential, he said.
The economy is still expected to grow 2.3% this year, he said, adding that the central bank would focus on addressing structural issues.
Southeast Asia's second-largest economy expanded 2.4% last year, lagging peers.
Vitai said the BOT plans a broad overhaul of non-bank regulations, including a new licensing regime for buy now, pay later services, with a public consultation expected by the year-end.

Buy now, pay later services will be regulated as personal loans, with the legal borrower age set at 18 to 20 years, credit limits capped at 20,000 baht ($606) and interest rates at 15% to 20%, he added.
